n99878f81c20.s: Under the basic principles of UN peacekeeping, force may be used only:
o: In self-defence and defence of the mandate
To secure political compliance of the parties
To enforce a settlement without consent of the parties
At the request of the troop-contributing country
n99878f81c20.x: The principles allow no use of force except in self-defence and defence of the mandate; force for political compliance is not a principle.

nd9cf68ba108.s: Which UN department manages peacekeeping missions?
o: Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs
Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
nd9cf68ba108.x: The Department of Peace Operations manages UN peacekeeping missions, which are funded through a separate assessment scale.

nd3f78411633.s: The Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) programme was launched on:
nd3f78411633.x: ITEC was launched on 15 September 1964 as a training-based capacity-building programme; e-ITEC is its online form.

n0d061a34544.s: The Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR) was set up in 1950 by:
n0d061a34544.x: ICCR was set up in 1950 by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad; 1982 is the year of the first Festival of India, not of ICCR.

n93b67300fa0.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the EXIM Bank of India is correctly matched?
n93b67300fa0.x: EXIM Bank was established on 1 January 1982 under the EXIM Bank Act, 1981; its headquarters is in Mumbai, not New Delhi.

nb986ad1334d.s: Which of the following is one of the four Ds of the Modi Doctrine?
nb986ad1334d.x: The four Ds are Democracy, Demography, Demand and Diaspora; Development is not one of them.

n6dd74b11c59.s: The Information Fusion Centre – Indian Ocean Region (IFC-IOR), set up in December 2018, is located at:
n6dd74b11c59.x: IFC-IOR is at Gurugram, not Visakhapatnam; it serves maritime domain awareness and information sharing.

ncee24694ce6.s: The IMO-backed Djibouti Code of Conduct against piracy was adopted in:
ncee24694ce6.x: The Djibouti Code of Conduct was adopted in 2009; India joined it as an observer in 2020.

nded0a401903.s: The headquarters of the Eastern Naval Command, India's largest naval command, is at:
nded0a401903.x: The Eastern Naval Command is headquartered at Visakhapatnam, facing the Bay of Bengal, and is India's largest naval command.

n147b48901d8.s: India develops the Shahid Beheshti terminal at Chabahar port through:
n147b48901d8.x: India develops the Shahid Beheshti terminal through India Ports Global Ltd (IPGL).

ncd719d68990.s: India imports about what share of its crude oil needs?
ncd719d68990.x: India imports about 88% of its crude oil needs; about 50% is the share of natural gas imported.

nf105d033001.s: The ITBP guards the high-altitude China border from the Karakoram Pass to:
nf105d033001.x: The ITBP, raised in 1962, guards the China border from Karakoram Pass to Jachep La, with posts at 9,000–18,800 feet.

n76d01342745.s: Which border guarding force was raised in 1835?
n76d01342745.x: Assam Rifles was raised in 1835; the BSF dates from 1965, the ITBP from 1962 and the SSB from 1963.

n0f832a9ac0a.s: The Vibrant Villages Programme-II (VVP-II) runs from:
n0f832a9ac0a.x: VVP-II runs from 2024-25 to 2028-29 and covers villages on the Pakistan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Nepal and Bhutan borders.

nab46d802251.s: The United Liberation Front of Asom (ULFA) is an insurgent group based in:
nab46d802251.x: ULFA is based in Assam; NSCN is based in Nagaland and the People's War Group in Andhra Pradesh.

n9959d6ca00c.s: In Punjab and West Bengal, the BSF's jurisdiction inside the international border was extended from 15 km to:
n9959d6ca00c.x: BSF jurisdiction in Punjab and West Bengal was extended from 15 km to 50 km; States objected as Police and Public Order are in the State List.

ndce4ebd3b62.s: In the three-tier coastal-security arrangement after 26/11, shallow waters are the responsibility of the:
ndce4ebd3b62.x: Coastal police cover shallow waters, the Coast Guard territorial waters, and the Navy has overall responsibility.

n674bc98e3ae.s: India's external intelligence agency, the Research and Analysis Wing (RAW), functions under:
n674bc98e3ae.x: RAW, established in 1968, functions under the Cabinet Secretariat.

n50151d26ce0.x: TADA was enacted in 1985 and lapsed in 1995.

n51346ed55e3.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the People's War Group is correctly matched?
n51346ed55e3.x: PWG was founded in 1980 by Kondapalli Seetharamaiah, was based in Andhra Pradesh and merged into the CPI (Maoist) in 2004.

new.s: The Centre for UN Peacekeeping (CUNPK), run by the Indian Army, is located in:
new.x: CUNPK, New Delhi, trains over 10,000 personnel a year, about 2,000 of them foreigners.

new.s: The UN mission UNMISET (2002-2005) was deployed in:
new.x: UNMISET was in Timor-Leste; UNMIL was in Liberia, MINUSTAH in Haiti and UNMISS is in South Sudan.

new.s: UNIFIL, a UN peacekeeping mission running since 1978, is in:
new.x: UNIFIL is in Lebanon; UNDOF is on the Golan Heights, MONUSCO in DR Congo and UNMISS in South Sudan.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a UN peacekeeping force?
new.x: The IPKF (Sri Lanka, Operation Pawan) was an Indian force, not a UN force.

new.s: India's largest contingent in UN peacekeeping history was in which mission?
new.x: India's largest contingent served in ONUC in the Congo (1960-64).

new.s: The Metro Express, an Indian grant project, is located in:
new.x: Metro Express and the Supreme Court building are Indian grant projects in Mauritius; Salma Dam is in Afghanistan.

new.s: India's $1 billion Line of Credit announced in 2020 was for:
new.x: India announced a $1 billion Line of Credit for Central Asia in 2020.

new.s: Operation Dost (2023) was India's relief operation for:
new.x: Operation Dost was for the Türkiye-Syria earthquake; Maitri was Nepal, Kaveri Sudan and Ajay Israel.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Sankat Mochan (2016) was South Sudan; Ganga was Ukraine, Ajay Israel and Maitri the Nepal earthquake.

new.s: The first country to adopt India's UPI, in July 2021, was:
new.x: Bhutan was the first to adopt UPI (July 2021); Sri Lanka and Mauritius followed in 2024.

new.s: Which was the first European country to launch UPI, in 2024?
new.x: France became the first country in Europe to launch UPI, in 2024.

new.s: The 18th Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (8-10 January 2025) was held at:
new.x: The 18th PBD was held at Bhubaneswar; Indore hosted the 17th, Varanasi the 15th and Gandhinagar the 13th.

new.s: Since 2015, the Pravasi Bharatiya Divas convention has been held:
new.x: PBD has been biennial since 2015.

new.s: In 2024, India's rank among the world's remittance-receiving countries was:
new.x: India is the top remittance recipient, receiving about $129 billion in 2024.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian diaspora:
1. India received about $129 billion in remittances in 2024.
2. Indian-born people are now Australia's largest immigrant community.
3. The UAE hosts about 3.5 million Indians.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: All three are correct: India received about $129 billion in 2024, Indian-born people are Australia's largest immigrant community, and the UAE hosts about 3.5 million Indians.

new.s: The first Festival of India was held in 1982 in:
new.x: The first Festival of India was in the UK (1982); the USA and France followed in 1985-86 and the USSR in 1987-88.

new.s: The UN General Assembly resolution establishing the International Day of Yoga was adopted on:
new.x: The UNGA resolution was adopted on 11 December 2014; the first Yoga Day was in 2015.

new.s: The Study in India programme, launched in 2018, is run by the Ministry of:
new.x: Study in India was launched in 2018 by the Education Ministry.

new.s: The online form of India's ITEC training programme is known as:
new.x: e-ITEC is the online form of the ITEC training programme.

new.s: SHANTI is India's security framework for the:
new.x: SHANTI is India's Bay of Bengal security framework, alongside SAGAR and MAHASAGAR.

new.s: The 9th Indian Ocean Conference, organised by the India Foundation, was held in:
new.x: The Indian Ocean Conference, held since 2016 by the India Foundation, had its 9th edition in Mauritius.

new.s: MILAN, the Indian Navy exercise first held at Port Blair in 1995, is a:
o: Trilateral exercise with Japan and the USA
new.x: MILAN is a multilateral Indian Navy exercise, first held at Port Blair in 1995, not a bilateral one.

new.s: The first AIKEYME exercise with African navies was held in 2025 in:
new.x: AIKEYME, India's exercise with African navies, was first held in 2025 in Tanzania.

new.s: The IOS SAGAR mission of 2026 sailed from Mumbai on board:
new.x: IOS SAGAR sailed on INS Sunayna; INS Sumedha carried the President at the 2026 Fleet Review.

new.s: Australia joined the Malabar naval exercise, making it a Quad exercise, in:
new.x: Malabar began as India-US in 1992; Japan became permanent in 2015 and Australia joined in 2020.

new.s: The Kaladan project links Kolkata to Mizoram through which Myanmar port?
new.x: The Kaladan route runs Kolkata – Sittwe – Paletwa – Mizoram.

new.s: India joined the Ashgabat Agreement, signed in 2011, in:
new.x: The Ashgabat Agreement dates from 2011; India joined it in 2018.

new.s: The western branch of the International North-South Transport Corridor passes through:
new.x: The INSTC (2000; India, Iran, Russia) has a western branch through Azerbaijan.

new.s: India's operating contract for Chabahar's Shahid Beheshti terminal, signed in May 2024, is for:
new.x: The May 2024 contract is for 10 years, not 20.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Chabahar port:
1. It lies in Sistan-Baluchestan on the Gulf of Oman.
2. It gives India access to Afghanistan and Central Asia bypassing Pakistan.
3. Its terminal was damaged in the US strikes of July 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; statement 3 is wrong because the terminal was not damaged in the July 2026 US strikes.

new.s: India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves are at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and:
new.x: India's SPRs are at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur, with 5.33 MMT capacity.

new.s: India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves cover about how many days of demand?
new.x: India's SPR covers about 9.5 days, against the IEA norm of 90 days.

new.s: Which country is the only one storing crude oil in India's Strategic Petroleum Reserve?
new.x: The UAE, India's 4th crude supplier, is the only country storing oil in India's SPR.

new.s: The 'One Sun One World One Grid' initiative is associated with the:
new.x: One Sun One World One Grid is linked with the International Solar Alliance, headquartered at Gurugram.

new.s: Duqm, a port giving India strategic access, is in:
new.x: Duqm is in Oman; Sabang is in Indonesia, Agalega in Mauritius and Sittwe in Myanmar.

new.s: China's first overseas military base, set up in 2017, is at:
new.x: Djibouti hosts China's first overseas base (2017) and the US Camp Lemonnier.

new.s: Diego Garcia in the Indian Ocean hosts a military base of:
new.x: Diego Garcia is a US-UK base; a UK-Mauritius treaty on it was signed in May 2025.

new.s: Under UNCLOS, the Exclusive Economic Zone extends up to:
new.x: The EEZ extends to 200 nm; 12 nm is the territorial sea, 24 nm the contiguous zone and 350 nm the outer shelf limit.

new.s: Of the 25,602 sq km disputed area, the 2014 PCA award gave Bangladesh about:
new.x: The 2014 PCA award gave Bangladesh 19,467 of the 25,602 sq km.

new.s: Matsya-6000 is part of India's:
new.x: Matsya-6000 and Samudrayaan are under the Deep Ocean Mission.

new.s: At the International Fleet Review 2026 at Visakhapatnam, President Murmu reviewed the fleet aboard:
new.x: The President reviewed the 2026 IFR aboard INS Sumedha; INS Sunayna carried IOS SAGAR.

new.s: Before 2026, Visakhapatnam last hosted the International Fleet Review in:
new.x: Visakhapatnam hosted the IFR in 2016 and again in 2026.

new.s: Which is India's newest border guarding force?
new.x: The SSB, guarding Nepal (2001) and Bhutan (2004), is the newest border force; Assam Rifles is the oldest.

new.s: The Assam Rifles guards India's border with:
new.x: Assam Rifles guards the Myanmar border, not Bangladesh, which is with the BSF.

new.s: The CRPF began on 27 July 1939 as the:
new.x: The CRPF began on 27 July 1939 as the Crown Representative's Police.

new.s: Operation Cactus (1988) was India's intervention in:
new.x: Operation Cactus (1988) reversed a coup in the Maldives.

new.s: The C-60 anti-Naxal commandos operate in:
new.x: The C-60 commandos are Gadchiroli's (Maharashtra) anti-Naxal force.

new.s: Jaish-e-Mohammed was founded by:
new.x: Masood Azhar founded Jaish-e-Mohammed; Hafiz Saeed (with Zafar Iqbal) founded Lashkar-e-Taiba.

new.s: The Resistance Front (TRF) is a proxy of:
new.x: TRF is a proxy of Lashkar-e-Taiba.

new.s: NSCN was founded in 1980 by Isak Chishi Swu, Th. Muivah and:
new.x: NSCN was founded by Isak Chishi Swu, Th. Muivah and S.S. Khaplang; Baruah and Rajkhowa are ULFA leaders.

new.s: The terrorist attack on India's Parliament took place on:
new.x: The Parliament attack was on 13 December 2001.

new.s: POTA, enacted in 2002, was repealed in:
new.x: POTA was enacted in 2002 and repealed in 2004; 2008 is the year of the NIA Act.

new.s: The 2019 amendment to the UAPA allowed:
o: Individuals to be designated as terrorists
new.x: The 2019 UAPA amendment allows individuals to be designated as terrorists.

new.s: India's first National Counter-Terrorism Policy was released by the MHA in:
new.x: The MHA released India's first National Counter-Terrorism Policy in December 2025.

new.s: The base of Andhra Pradesh's Greyhounds force is at:
new.x: The Greyhounds, raised in 1989, are based at Anandapuram (Visakhapatnam).

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Greyhounds:
1. It is Andhra Pradesh's force against left-wing extremism.
2. It cut Naxal activity in Alluri Sitharama Raju and Parvathipuram Manyam districts.
3. It broke red corridors on the Andhra-Odisha Border.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: All three are correct: the Greyhounds fight left-wing extremism, cut Naxal activity in those districts and broke red corridors on the AOB.

new.s: The maximum age for the Chief of Defence Staff is:
new.x: The CDS can serve up to a maximum age of 65.

new.s: The Chief of Defence Staff heads which department of the Ministry of Defence?
new.x: The CDS heads the Department of Military Affairs in the MoD.

new.s: Who chairs the Defence Acquisition Council?
new.x: The Defence Minister, not the CDS, chairs the Defence Acquisition Council.

new.s: NATGRID functions under the:
new.x: NATGRID is under the MHA, not the MEA.

new.s: CERT-In functions under the:
new.x: CERT-In is under MeitY; RAW is under the Cabinet Secretariat and IB under the MHA.

new.s: Commandos of the National Security Guard (NSG) are popularly called:
new.x: NSG, under the MHA, is known as the 'Black Cats'; Greyhounds and C-60 are State anti-Naxal forces.

new.s: The Golden Triangle of drug production comprises Myanmar, Laos and:
new.x: The Golden Triangle is Myanmar, Laos and Thailand, not Bangladesh.

new.s: In terror financing, FICN refers to:
new.x: FICN is fake Indian currency, used alongside hawala and narcotics for terror financing.

new.s: India shares its shortest international land border with:
new.x: The Afghanistan border (106 km) is the shortest; Bangladesh (4,096.7 km) is the longest.

new.s: Phase I of the Vibrant Villages Programme covers villages on the border with:
new.x: Phase I covers China-border states; VVP-II covers the Pakistan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Nepal and Bhutan borders.

new.s: Sagar Kavach is a:
new.x: Sagar Kavach is a biannual coastal-security exercise.

new.s: How many marine police stations were sanctioned for Andhra Pradesh in Phase I (2005) of the Coastal Security Scheme?
new.x: Six marine police stations were sanctioned for AP in Phase I (2005); 15 had been sanctioned by 2022.
